messages:
Chris Nguyen: Thanks everyone for joining the infra section of the all-hands earlier. Quick follow-up thread for clarifying GPU regions, autoscaling behavior, and next steps. Drop questions and we’ll answer live. :wave:
Olivia Park: Thanks — quick one: APAC timeline? I heard APAC dev zones might slip. Is procurement blocking or just config?
Anika Bose: Two things: 1) if GPU supply tight, what’s our fallback (cheaper quantized variants, cross-region routing?), and 2) how will SLOs be preserved during bursts?
David Romero: For Dedicated customers — are we still guaranteeing pinned capacity for Q3 customers who signed the contract last month? Need wording for legal.
Leo Zhang: Autoscaler question: will policy be model-aware (e.g., different batch targets for embeddings vs chat) or just node-level CPU/GPU util thresholds?
Infra Bot: deploy-bot: Autoscaler v2 rollout started for staging at 2026-06-03T14:22Z — jobs queued: 4, expected window 30m.
Mike Patel: Also, telemetry — will Console show token-level cost after we enable aggressive batching? Ops needs to see before/after cost per-route.
Rachel Kim: Any cost estimate for switching to 4-bit quantization across r5 models? Even rough percent helps product.
Priya Singh: For rollouts: can we do canary per-region (start US-East, then EMEA, then APAC) or do we need global flags?
Chris Nguyen: Good set. Short answers now, follow-up doc + owners after.
Chris Nguyen: APAC timeline — procurement lead says hardware orders placed but lead times vary by vendor. Realistic earliest: late Q3 for APAC zones, likely phased (compute first, specialized interconnects follow).
Chris Nguyen: Fallbacks — yes: 1) model-variant routing to smaller/quantized checkpoints, 2) cross-region routing for latency-tolerant customers, 3) queued bursts with graceful degradation (shorter context or rate-limit escalation).
Chris Nguyen: Dedicated contracts — we will honor pinned capacity. Customer agreements signed before capacity re-sell cutoff get priority placement; legal will get the precise clause. @David Romero can you share contract IDs offline?
Leo Zhang: @Chris Nguyen got it — are autoscaler rules going to look at `estimated_tokens_per_sec` or just GPU utilization?
Chris Nguyen: Autoscaler v2 will be hybrid. We plan to expose model-aware heuristics: estimated token throughput and model profile + GPU util. Initial shipping: node-level util + per-model weight hints; full-profile aware in v2.1.
Anika Bose: Can you paste the sample policy snippet? Even a toy one helps engineering.
Chris Nguyen: Sure — example below (toy):
```
policy:
  - name: burst-scale-up
    trigger: token_rate > 50000 OR gpu_util > 0.78
    action: add_nodes: 2, prefer_region: same
  - name: maintain-slo
    trigger: p99_latency > 500ms
    action: route_fallback: smaller_variant
```
Chris Nguyen: That is simplified — real config will include model_weight, priority_class, and cooldown windows.
Mike Patel: For telemetry: yes, Console will receive a batching/cost delta view in the next console release. You’ll be able to filter by route/model and see estimated cost per 1k tokens with/without batching.
Rachel Kim: Any rough savings number for 4-bit quant across large-gen checkpoints?
Chris Nguyen: Early numbers from research: 4-bit post-training quantization gives ~25-35% throughput improvement on certain kernels, and memory reduction ~40%. Effect on quality varies — we’ll tie to evals before recommending wide rollout.
Priya Singh: Canary plan?
Chris Nguyen: Canary per-region is the plan. We’ll flip region-level flags so we can iterate region-by-region. If we see regressions, automatic rollback to previous variant.
Olivia Park: If APAC slips to late Q3, can we mitigate by temporarily routing APAC traffic to US-West with an explicit customer opt-in? Latency hit but keeps app alive.
Chris Nguyen: Yes — we have a routing policy that can be enabled per-customer for cross-region fallback. Need product sign-off for default behavior (opt-in vs opt-out).
David Romero: Sending the contract list to legal now. Thanks.
Anika Bose: Follow-up: who owns the autoscaler SLO dashboard? Need contact to add tests.
Chris Nguyen: @Leo Zhang will own the initial SLO dashboard. Leo, can you coordinate with DevEx to add synthetic tests?
Leo Zhang: Yep — will create a tracking ticket and share the dashboard link once skeleton is up.
Infra Bot: incident-bot: new ticket created #INF-4712 "autoscaler canary monitoring" assigned to Leo Zhang.
Chris Nguyen: Next steps: I’ll post a short doc with timeline and owners (link coming). We’ll have a sync next Tuesday 10am PT for teams doing rollouts. If you need urgent support, ping me or @Priya Singh. :thumbsup:
Priya Singh: Thanks — adding a short agenda item for ops readiness.
Olivia Park: Thanks, leaving a comment in the doc once posted.
Mike Patel: Great, having the cost deltas in Console will help get buy-in from Finance.
Rachel Kim: Thx — can we also add a note about which evals we’ll use to guard quality when enabling quant?
Chris Nguyen: Will include eval suite and owners in the doc. Appreciate the questions.
Chris Nguyen: Closing thread once doc is live, will bump here.
